children.label: a
children.prompt: Write down the formula for the area of a triangle.

answer.worked:
$$A=\frac{bh}{2}$$
Here $b$ is the base and $h$ is the perpendicular height.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The area of a triangle is $8\text{ cm}^{2}$.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find the height of the triangle if the base is $10\text{ cm}$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Find the height of the triangle if it is equal to the base.

answer.worked:
The base equals the height, so $b=h$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\8&=\frac{h^{2}}{2}\\h^{2}&=16\\h&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The height must be positive.

entries.description:
Solving Quadratic Equations
We can use formulas to find any unknown value when we know all other quantities.
1. Write the formula.
2. Substitute given values.
3. Solve for the unknown value using inverse operations.

entries.description: Example Substitute values into a formula to find the unknown

presentation.arrangement: Two side-by-side examples; direct substitution on the left, solving for the squared variable on the right.

entries.description:
A = 3x²
Find A when x = 6.
1. Write formula: A = 3x²
2. Substitute: A = 3(6)²
3. Solve: A = 108

entries.ambiguity: The prose uses lowercase l, whereas the formula and diagram use uppercase L. Normalize the prose to L so students can identify the same length variable.

resolution.reason: Retain the existing normalized uppercase L in the editable stem. It matches the source formula and diagram and prevents students from interpreting l and L as different variables. No further correction is needed.
